note.explanation: A computer network links devices so they can exchange data and work together. Nodes are the connected devices, and links connect those nodes. Switches forward data within a network; routers connect different networks. Networks help people share resources, communicate, and collaborate.
examples: Several office computers share one printer.
Employees at different locations meet through video conferencing.
note.checkAnswer: A switch forwards data between nodes within a network.
note.simple: A network is a group of connected devices that can share information and resources.

note.title: Network as a System
steps: Identify the nodes: these are devices connected to the network.
Identify the links: these connect the nodes, either by wire or wirelessly.
Use switches to forward data within a network.
Use routers to connect different networks and direct data packets.

written.text: Q6.1. Discuss the objectives of computer networks and provide examples of how they facilitate resource sharing and data communication.
written.finalAnswer: The primary objectives of computer networks are resource sharing, data communication and collaboration. Networks allow devices to share resources, such as printers and storage. For example, multiple office computers can share a single printer. Networks also facilitate communication through email, instant messaging and video conferencing. For example, employees in different locations can collaborate through video conferencing tools.

rubric.description: Identifies resource sharing, data communication and collaboration as objectives.
rubric.how: State all three objectives of computer networks.

rubric.description: Explains data communication and names suitable communication methods.

rubric.description: Gives an example of people using a network to communicate or collaborate.
rubric.how: Give the example of employees in different locations collaborating through video conferencing.

modelAnswer: The primary objectives of computer networks are resource sharing, data communication and collaboration.
Resource sharing: Computer networks allow devices to share resources, such as printers and storage, reducing costs and improving efficiency.
Example: In an office network, multiple computers can share a single printer, reducing the need for multiple printers.
Data communication: Networks facilitate data transfer, enabling communication through emails, instant messaging, and video conferencing.
Example: Employees in different locations can collaborate through video conferencing tools like Zoom or Microsoft Teams.
Connectivity and collaboration: Networks connect devices, allowing for remote access and collaboration, improving productivity and flexibility.
Example: A team can work on a shared document in real-time using cloud-based services like Google Drive.

examTips: A short question may ask you to define a computer network or explain the role of a switch or router. Use the textbook's precise definition or state the device's job clearly.
A long question may ask for the objectives of computer networks with examples. Name the objectives, explain each one, and give the textbook-style example.
For a question about components, distinguish nodes (connected devices), links (connections), switches (forward data within a network) and routers (connect different networks).
Examples earn marks when they clearly match the objective: a shared printer shows resource sharing, while video conferencing shows data communication.

steps.why: The section compares passengers with the data being sent.
steps.text: When traveling, passengers (data) might be split into groups (packets) and assigned different flights (paths). In packet switching each group has a ticket with the final destination (IP address).

steps.why: This connects the different routes in the example to the devices that direct data across networks.
steps.text: These groups might take different routes, through various airports (routers), to reach the final destination.

example.question: EXAMPLE: Air Travel System — How does sending people via air travel relate to packet switching?
example.answer: Data can be split into packets, and the packets may take different routes through routers to reach the final destination.

explain.title: A computer network is a system
explain.body: A computer network is a system of linked devices and computers that may exchange data and operate together. This is the textbook definition. Networks can be small, like a LAN, or large, like a WAN or the Internet.

explain.title: Nodes and links
explain.body: Nodes: Devices that are connected to the network, such as computers, smartphones, and printers. Links: The connections between nodes, which can be wired (like Ethernet cables) or wireless (like Wi-Fi).

explain.title: Switches and routers
explain.body: Switches: Devices that connect multiple nodes within a network to forward data. Routers: Devices that connect different networks and direct data packets between them. A switch forwards data within a network; a router directs data between networks.

explain.title: Objectives of networks
explain.body: The primary objective of computer network is to enable resource sharing, data communication and collaboration. A shared office printer is an example of resource sharing. Email, instant messaging and video conferencing are examples of data communication.

mistakes: Do not swap the jobs of a switch and a router: a switch connects nodes within a network; a router connects different networks.
Do not describe a node as a connection. A node is a connected device; a link is the connection between nodes.
When asked for objectives, do not list only resource sharing. Include data communication and collaboration as well.
Give examples that match the objective: a shared printer is resource sharing; video conferencing is data communication.
Do not confuse a network with the Internet. The Internet is the largest network, connecting networks worldwide.
